title.value: Generate editable website designs in Figma from the terminal

introduction.value:
A designer spent 3 days using Claude Code with Figma to generate a band website as an editable file and pick matching images for an e-commerce prototype.
·
Nov 9, 2026

method.value: A UX designer set up Claude Code in the terminal with the Claude desktop app linked to project folders. Claude generated websites, including one for a favourite band, and the designer copied them into Figma as editable files. After editing in Figma, the designer sent a Figma link back to Claude, which worked out the changes. For an e-commerce prototype, one terminal prompt made Claude pull in matching product images and generate filters.

outcome.value: Round-tripping worked well, and the same loop made mobile layouts quick. First designs all looked like generic dark themes, and Claude put new pages onto the home page instead of building separate ones. Browser edits were slow.

notes.value: Make visual edits in Figma and go back to Claude only when finished, because small colour or text changes through prompts were slow.

source_text.body:
Generate editable website designs in Figma from the terminal
A designer spent 3 days using Claude Code with Figma to generate a band website as an editable file and pick matching images for an e-commerce prototype.
·
Nov 9, 2026
Done with
CC
Claude Code
CL
Claude
What they did
A UX designer set up Claude Code in the terminal with the Claude desktop app linked to project folders. Claude generated websites, including one for a favourite band, and the designer copied them into Figma as editable files. After editing in Figma, the designer sent a Figma link back to Claude, which worked out the changes. For an e-commerce prototype, one terminal prompt made Claude pull in matching product images and generate filters.
How it went
Round-tripping worked well, and the same loop made mobile layouts quick. First designs all looked like generic dark themes, and Claude put new pages onto the home page instead of building separate ones. Browser edits were slow.
Worth knowing
Make visual edits in Figma and go back to Claude only when finished, because small colour or text changes through prompts were slow.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Using my Figma connection, generate an editable website design for [band, brand or project name] with a [mood, e.g. dark, gritty, minimal] look. Build the home page and [other pages, e.g. tour, shop] as editable frames, and pick matching images for [e-commerce items or sections]. You are done when every page is in Figma as editable layers and you have listed where the images came from.
Original source: https://medium.com/design-bootcamp/my-experience-with-claude-code-terminal-and-figma-so-far-4cc9ca5e39a7
